answer: Coordinated Action Surcharge. Each agent claims a coordination slot by paying a fee that scales with the number of slots claimed in the same epoch, so a thousand sybils cost superlinearly more than one. The fee is redistributed to agents who act alone, creating an echo of lost value for clustered identities. An attacker must sustain rising costs per fake agent, capped by an ivory audit trail of slot ownership. A reef of independent actors then outcompetes the swarm, since genuine coordination surfaces as costly, not free.
